title: Little-Moved by Huge Drop in Oil and Tech Stocks
summary:
Little-Moved by Huge Drop in Oil and Tech Stocks 

             
             
            Bonds were technically stronger at 4pm ET, but just barely. Over the past 2 sessions, we've seen Treasury yields noticeably disconnect from the prevailing correlation with tech stocks. This began after the opening bell last Friday and mostly continued today. Bonds were generally improving while the NASDAQ was higher for most of the day and then sold off starting at 1pm when tech stocks saw their biggest losses (i.e. the opposite of the prevailing correlation). Part of the credit for the bond selling goes to the market's takeaway from Treasury's preliminary borrowing estimates which were $24 billion higher than expected before adjusting for estimated cash balances. Some of the earlier strength in bonds aligned with a sharp decline in oil. While it's true that oil has been the opposite of a reliable source of inspiration for bonds, today's drop was sharp enough to possibly make an exception.

title: Mortgage Rates Hold Steady at Recent Lows
summary: It was a perfectly fine day for mortgage rates to start the new week. The underlying bond market improved modestly, drawing on a combination of sharply lower oil prices and another drop in tech-related stocks.  While it's true that oil prices haven't had a reliable impact on bonds/rates over the past month, today's drop was big enough that is probably helped to some extent, especially when we consider some headwinds created by updated borrowing estimates released by the U.S. Treasury today.  Once per quarter, Treasury updates estimated Treasury auction amounts. Treasuries are the foundation of almost all interest rates in the U.S. When supply increases or demand falls, it puts downward pressure on prices and upward pressure on rates, all else equal.  Today's upward pressure was fairly modest, but still noticeable. Mortgage lenders played it fairly safe by setting today's rates perfectly in line with last Friday's. That makes today tied for the lowest 30yr fixed level since September 23rd, 2026.

title: Broker, Home Equity, Verification, M&A Data; Legal Issue Conference; Non-Agency Product News
summary: Sometimes you and your teammates have different priorities. I head to Dallas tomorrow for a private mortgage event, where the priorities will probably be mostly aligned. Besides the election, and perhaps the inflation-beating Costco’s Thanksgiving meal, the profitability of HELOCs, 2nd mortgages, and equity products in general will definitely be a discussion topic. In the past much of this product (85 percent by some estimates) was held by banks. Now that is estimated to be down to 65 percent, and non-banks of all shapes and sizes are coming on strong, market-share-wise. Besides having decent margins, some will say these products are the best recapture tool today. While this is going on, the adjustable-rate market is still… a jumble? (Remember the saying, popular with some, “Date the rate, marry the house.”?) Borrowers with 3-1, 5-1, 7-1s that are adjusting are in for a rude awakening, simultaneously leading to LOs having to explain rates but also potentially leading to a lead source for nimble originators. (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by FirstClose, which helps financial institutions grow a successful home equity business with innovative solutions that minimize application drop-off, automate time-consuming processes, and reduce time to close from weeks to days. Today’s has an interview with Keynova’s Beth Robertson on growing competition and innovation in digital home equity lending, emphasizing faster applications, real-time prequalification, transparent pricing, and streamlined, personalized customer experiences as key differentiators for lenders.)

title: Slightly Stronger Start. Mostly Holding After ISM Data
summary: Bonds were initially a hair weaker at the start of the overnight session, but rallied gradually after that. The sharpest gains arrived at the 9:30am NYSE open, suggesting money manager reallocations and "new month" trades. ISM Manufacturing hit 30 minutes later and the first reaction was modest bounce toward slightly higher yields and slightly higher stock prices. Perhaps the most notable development is that stocks are back up to Friday morning's levels even as bonds remain 4-5bps lower compared to the same baseline.

title: eLEND Lowers Credit Score Floors To 500 On FHA Cash-Out Loans
summary: eLEND is lowering minimum credit score requirements on select FHA cash-out refinances and conventional loans through the end of the year, joining a growing number of lenders easing restrictions to reach borrowers who previously fell outside their lending guidelines.The Parsippany, New Jersey-based lender announced Monday that its new CreditEdge program will accept FHA cash-out refinances with decision credit scores of 500 to 579, along with select conventional purchase and rate-and-term refinance loans with scores below 620, subject to automated underwriting approval.

title: Midterms Loom With Mortgage Policy Changes Already In Motion
summary: Housing affordability has become a major issue heading into Tuesday's midterm elections. But for mortgage lenders and originators, some of the decisions that could matter most in 2027 are already underway, regardless of which party controls Congress.The Trump administration is pursuing changes to refinancing costs and mortgage insurance cancellation, while the Mortgage Bankers Association is pushing for lower credit-reporting expenses, more flexible loan officer compensation rules, and reductions in government-backed loan costs.

title: UWM Expands VantageScore Into Non-Agency Lending
summary: United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM)  is extending VantageScore eligibility to select non-agency loans, bringing its dual-credit-score approach to jumbo, bank statement, investor, and home equity products where minimum credit-score requirements remain in place.The move extends UWM's push into specialty lending while giving brokers another way to qualify borrowers who may fall short of a program's credit-score threshold under Classic FICO.

title: Dark Matter Expands AI Ambitions With House Numbers Acquisition
summary: Dark Matter Technologies is taking another step toward automating mortgage production, acquiring an artificial intelligence platform capable of working loan conditions, communicating with borrowers, and performing tasks that have traditionally required loan officers and processors.The company announced Friday that it acquired the AI agent platform and related intellectual property of House Numbers, a venture-backed technology company whose autonomous agents have been operating on live mortgage files for two years.

title: VantageScore Names Interim CEO Amid Growing Mortgage Market Presence
summary: VantageScore has named Anthony Hutchinson interim president and CEO following the departure of Silvio Tavares, placing a veteran housing finance executive at the helm as the credit-scoring company gains ground in the mortgage market and intensifies its competition with FICO.Hutchinson, who previously led VantageScore's public affairs and government relations efforts, takes over after five years under Tavares, during which the company more than tripled its market presence and secured a larger role in mortgage credit scoring.
